acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given a financial snapshot and payment allocation for a month, when I run the projection generator, then for each month it calculates: starting balance per account, interest charged, payment applied, principal paid, ending balance, running total debt.
Projection continues until all debts reach zero OR maximum 360 months (30 years) is reached.
Projection handles accounts being paid off by skipping further calculations for zero-balance accounts.
When payment exceeds remaining balance, payment is capped at balance (no overpayment).
Output is an array of MonthlyProjection objects containing per-account snapshots and totals.
All calculations use big.js for precision with cent-level accuracy (2 decimal places in ZAR).
The projection generator accepts a PaymentAllocator function that determines how surplus is distributed across accounts (enabling different strategy implementations).
Unit tests verify projection correctness against manual spreadsheet calculations for 2-account scenarios.

constraints.constraint: All calculations use big.js for cent-level precision (ADR-003)
Strategy implementations follow Strategy Pattern (ADR-004) with common DebtStrategy interface
Framework-agnostic design in src/lib/calculations/ - no React imports
Projection generator is called by EACH strategy, so efficiency matters - avoid unnecessary Big instances in loops
Use early termination when debt reaches zero
Clone accounts once at start, mutate in place during simulation
Reuse calculateMonthlyInterest() from interest.ts for interest calculations

tests.standards: Tests use Vitest as the testing framework (Vite-native, fast, TypeScript support). Tests are organized in tests/lib/calculations/ directory mirroring src/ structure. Each test file imports from @/ path alias. Tests verify against known spreadsheet calculations for accuracy. Use describe/it blocks with clear AC references in test descriptions. All calculation functions should be tested as pure functions - same inputs produce identical outputs.
